notes: All six required web searches ran this time; none returned any statement by Rep. Austin Scott (R-GA-8) about AI risk, superintelligence, extinction, a pause or slowdown, a China agreement, or AI safety. Results for the superintelligence, extinction and AI safety queries concerned other people (for example Rep. Greg Casar, and Scott Aaronson); the China query hit Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, a different person. The site-restricted search found only AI mentions from 2019 and 2020 (before the window) and a 25 February 2025 release announcing Congressional App Challenge winners (https://austinscott.house.gov/2025/2/rep-austin-scott-recognizes-congressional-app-challenge-winners), which describes a student's machine-learning app and contains nothing on AI risk; it was not opened and is not recorded as a statement. Earlier attempt (kept): his official site was opened directly, home page and press release pages 1 and 2 of 59 (https://austinscott.house.gov/press-releases), covering releases from 4 March 2025 to 23 July 2026; no title mentions AI, and the three NDAA releases (22 July 2026, 5 June 2026, 10 December 2025) do not mention AI. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: the FastDemocracy page for H.R. 10538 (https://fastdemocracy.com/bill-search/us/119/bills/USB00108512/, opened 14 November 2026) lists 12 cosponsors, all Democrats, and Austin Scott is not among them; Congress.gov itself was not checked (it returned HTTP 403 earlier). No House letter about AI risk led or signed by him was found outside the centrally handled multi-signer letters, which were not searched per instructions. Press releases after 23 July 2026, hearing transcripts and floor speeches were not checked individually beyond what the searches covered.
